summary.tautology_note: the verifiable subset is DEFINED by the presence of a numeric conflict, and the numeric detector is an OR-branch of the joint gate, so the joint gate's recall on this subset is 1.0 by construction and is not evidence. The informative quantity is 'conjunction_recall_on_verifiable_subset': how many of these conflicts the NLI-and-same-subject conjunction catches with the numeric branch removed, and therefore what the numeric branch adds.
summary.ground_truth_note: recall on the verifiable subset uses numeric conflicts, which are checkable by inspection and independent of the NLI model; the precision/recall figures below are against an NLI-derived PROXY and are therefore not independent of the detector
summary.precision_definition: 'joint_gate_precision' is NOT a precision against an independent ground truth, and after the subject-check repair it is not even a useful proxy: the 'true' set it is computed against is the gate's own set, because the proxy uses the gate's own subject rule. Its precision is therefore 1.000 and its false-positive rate 0.000 *by construction*, and neither number means anything. The measurement that is not circular is the reader labelling in Experiment 11, and the measurement that separates the mechanism from the corpus is the detector's own control in Experiment 11b. The corroboration shares below decompose the alarms between the branches and say nothing about whether the alarms are right.
summary.subject_check_rule: The same-subject check is the conjunction of the two signals its own design names: topical similarity AND shared concrete objects (part numbers, plant codes, distinctive quantities, and content words). The implementation used to let topical similarity through on its own, which on a corpus of articles about one subject made the check a topic check: two chunks of the same article about different sub-topics passed it. The reader labelling in Experiment 11 showed the consequence and the repair.
summary.revision_branch_rule: The revision branch is exact rather than statistical: it reads the version markers out of the text and fires when two passages name the same standard at two different issues and share a specific term. It is the branch this corpus can be evaluated on, because its correctness is a fact about the text rather than a judgement about it.
summary.numeric_branch_rule: A number is a quantity only when a measurement term governs it (the term is also the key the two passages must agree on), when it is not a bare four-digit year, and when it is not part of a hyphenated identifier; a measurement term that begins a proper name is not a measurement. The numeric branch also carries the same subject check as the conjunction branch. This replaced an earlier rule that keyed a number to the nearest distinctive word, which the reader-labelling experiment in Experiment 11 showed to fire on citation years, version numbers and surnames rather than on quantities.
summary.verifiable_subset_size_note: The verifiable subset now holds 0 pair(s). It was 21 pairs before the numeric rule was repaired. A subset this small cannot carry a recall measurement: the joint gate's recall on it is 1.0 by construction and, at this size, that number is arithmetic rather than evidence. The corpus is encyclopaedic prose about concepts, so it contains worked examples and formulae rather than instance-level data, and a quantity-conflict detector has almost nothing in it to find. The measurement that carries weight is the reader-labelled precision in Experiment 11, together with the alarm counts in this table.

numeric_rule_repair.note: The repair changed the detector, not the corpus, the benchmark or the label standard. The corpus is unchanged, the benchmark is unchanged, the seed is unchanged, and the rule was replaced by a measurement-keyed rule rather than tuned to a target. The quantity-level conflicts fell from 21 to 0 because the ones that fell were not conflicts: they were citation years, version numbers and surnames.

subject_check_repair.note: The second repair, forced by the same measurement: the same-subject check let topical similarity through on its own, although its own design says that two passages with high semantic similarity and no shared objects are almost always about different things. On a corpus of articles all about one subject that made the check a topic check, and it was the source of most of the alarms. Requiring shared concrete objects as well, as designed, cut the alarms from 76 to 20 and removed every alarm a reader had called a subject mismatch.
